title: Independent AI assurance and operating evidence
question: Which records show that AI assurance methods have been adopted, validated, and maintained for named operating systems?
why_it_matters: Risk frameworks and evaluation methods only become operating assurance when institutions select controls, test named systems, act on findings, monitor production behavior, and disclose outcomes.
current_support: FTFN now combines NIST assurance methods with GAO's 11-agency inventory analysis, IRS maturity and data-quality findings, GAO operational use cases, federal AI acquisition oversight, NASA active-use examples, and federal cyber-program implementation results.
missing_evidence: measured mission, safety, and reliability outcomes
candidate_records: full AI TEVV draft and final standard
agency system-level evaluation and authorization records
production monitoring, incident, and corrective-action evidence
next_action: Follow agency inventories and audits into named system usage, impact assessment, authorization, performance, incident, corrective-action, cost, mission-benefit, and retirement records.

named_records: GAO Generative AI Use and Management at Federal Agencies
GAO IRS AI Skills, Information Quality, and Strategic Management
GAO Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation Network Monitoring
latest_review.stage_result: The evidence now reaches inventory growth, operational examples, maturity gaps, acquisition oversight, and cyber-program implementation. Comparable system-level benefits and incidents remain incomplete.
latest_review.stop_rule: Do not treat inventory growth, active-use labels, acquisition, or cybersecurity-tool deployment as measured mission benefit or assurance.

notes: Phase 55Y creates a dedicated assurance gap so AI policy and procurement records are not mistaken for tested and maintained operation.
